#1693. Mikel Arteta hoping Man City charges saga doesn’t overshadow Arsenal clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has urged his Arsenal players to block out all talk of Manchester City’s Premier League charges and ensure they win the title on the pitch.

In September, City were were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, while an independent commission also ruled that the club failed to co-operate with an investigation.

An appeal has been submitted by City, who deny any wrongdoing, and it remains to be seen when a final resolution in the case will be reached.

It is a shadow hanging over the league ahead of Arsenal’s showdown with City in north London on Sunday.

Victory would move the Gunners nine points ahead of Enzo Maresca’s side and leave them in strong shape to defend their league title, regardless of any potential sanctions imposed on City.

Arteta is clear that his players cannot afford any distractions, demanding that they get the job done and defend their crown without relying on a potential points deduction for City.

“That’s the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on,” Arteta said. “There’s nothing else.”

Arsenal were defeated twice by City in the space of three weeks towards the end of last season, first in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley and then in a Premier League clash at the Etihad Stadium. Despite losing the latter game, Arsenal went on to win the title for the first time in 22 years.

A rivalry has built between the two clubs over the past five seasons, having gone toe-to-toe in several title races.

Asked if the guilty verdict against City and the wait for possible sanctions had diminished the significance of Sunday’s meeting, Arteta said: “I hope that it doesn’t because it’s a process that is still open.

“It’s not resolved and we don’t know what is going to happen. So, no, I think when we have two teams at the level that both teams are at right now with the quality players that are on that pitch, it’s a massive game and a big game to enjoy.”

However, when it was put to him that the atmosphere might be particularly emotional due to the strength of feeling from the Arsenal fans, Arteta sidestepped the topic.

“I don’t know,” he said. “That’s something very individual and I don’t want to go there.”

#1692. Ipswich Town vs Aston Villa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 18:48

Aston Villa travel to Portman Road to face Ipswich Town on Saturday evening seeking to climb back into the top half of the Premier League table.

Both meetings between these two sides during the 2024-25 season ended in entertaining draws (2-2 in Suffolk and 1-1 at Villa Park), leaving the Tractor Boys still searching for their first top-flight triumph over the Lions since February 1993.

Tipped by many to struggle before the season began, Ipswich are yet to spend a single day sitting in the Premier League relegation zone since securing promotion, but their recent form has seen them slip closer to the bottom three.

After winning three of their first six top-flight games this term (L3), the Tractor Boys have failed to come out on top in any of their last five fixtures (D2 L3), suffering defeats to Bournemouth (2-1) and Tottenham (2-0) either side of the international break.

Gary O'Neil acknowledged that his team “didn't get to our level enough” against Spurs and they now sit down in 16th place in the table, just two points above the drop zone with games against Villa, Coventry City, Leeds United, Newcastle United and Brighton & Hove Albion up next.

Another “soft” goal was conceded by Ipswich last time out, and they have now shipped a total of 22 goals in 11 Premier League matches – the third-most in the division – while they have failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last 30 top-flight games; only West Brom between August 2010 and May 2011 have endured a longer run in the division’s history (34 games).

Ipswich have also proved largely incapable of mounting second-half comebacks, failing to win any of the 22 Premier League matches in which they have trailed at half time since the start of the 2024-25 season (D3 L19). Striking first on Saturday could therefore be crucial for O'Neil’s side as they bid to upset Villa.

Since securing a 2-1 home victory over Man City on October 24, Aston Villa have failed to win any of their last six matches in all competitions (D3 L3), suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Unai Emery’s side previously played out a frustrating goalless stalemate at home to Sunderland in the Premier League, their third top-flight draw in a row that leaves them sitting 12th in the table and seven points behind fourth spot where they finished last season.

Villa – who have not drawn four consecutive Premier League matches since September 2011 – are preparing for a historic milestone on Saturday, as they play their 5,000th match across the top-four tiers of English football (W2,050 D1,199 L1,750), becoming the 16th club to reach the landmark.

Emery is keen to see his team rediscover their clinical touch in front of goal sooner rather than later, as Villa have failed to score in four of their last six games, not registering a single shot on target against Galatasaray.

Heading into Saturday’s clash in Suffolk, Villa have not lost any of their last 10 visits to Ipswich (D6 L3) in all competitions (W5 D4) since a 1-0 EFL Cup loss back in December 1992, while they are unbeaten in all 22 of their league matches against promoted sides under Emery (W15 D7).

Ipswich boss O'Neil has confirmed that Leif Davis has recovered from a knock to his ankle sustained in the defeat at Spurs, and the left-back will start this weekend.

Darnell Furlong started at right-back last time out, but O'Neil may be tempted to select either Abdoul Ouattara or Dara O'Shea on the right side of a four-man defence.

Zian Flemming was handed his first league start for Ipswich last time out, but he could be replaced up front by Emersonn, while Abdul Fatawu, Florentino Luis, Jack Clarke and Jacob Greaves will also be pushing to start after beginning as substitutes last weekend.

As for Aston Villa, Amadou Onana (knee) and Matteo Ruggeri (hamstring) remain sidelined through injury, but Matty Cash is available for selection after serving concussion protocols.

Cash is therefore expected to replace Taylor Harwood-Bellis and start at right-back, while Pau Torres is set to be recalled at centre-back at the expense of former Ipswich man Tyrone Mings.

With Alejandro Garnacho facing an uncertain future at Villa, Emery is likely to favour Alysson and Johan Manzambi in wide positions, providing support in attack for striker Nicolas Jackson who has netted six goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Walton; O'Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis; Lukic, Palacios; Clarke, Enciso, Maeda; Emersonn

Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Goretzka; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson

While Portman Road remains a far more forgiving environment for O'Neil’s side, who have collected seven of their 11 points on home soil this term (W2 D1 L2), Villa should relish the opportunity to rediscover their scoring touch against a porous Ipswich defence shipping an average of two goals per game.

Although the Tractor Boys are capable of keeping things competitive in Suffolk, we are backing Emery’s men to shake off their recent slump and grind out a hard-fought victory.

Liverpool are looking up as the hectic period of the campaign approaches.

Andoni Iraola's side have bounced back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce prior to the November international break, and go into the Everton game seeking a fourth straight win across all competitions.

While Sunday’s showdown at the Hill Dickinson Stadium will represent Iraola’s first taste of a Merseyside derby, history largely favours the Reds having lost just one of the last 10 meetings.

It remains to be seen if Victor Munoz is able to shake off a knock and prove his fitness, but two key Liverpool players will have to be careful if selected due to the looming threat of a ban.

With that in mind, here’s a look at the Liverpool players at risk of suspension.

As every club have already been made fully aware of this season, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Liverpool's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the home game against Coventry on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

Alexis Mac Allister and summer signing Bradley Barcola are the big suspensions concern for Liverpool at present.

The Argentina international was booked in the win over Crystal Palace so had to watch his step in the 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United, but Barcola is a new suspension risk after being cautioned in the second half last weekend.

As such, if the Frenchman and/or Mac Allister are shown a yellow card in the Merseyside derby, a one-match ban must be served in the very next fixture - at home to Sunderland on December 2.

Ultimately, the pair are walking the disciplinary tightrope for upcoming games against Everton, Sunderland, Chelsea, Leeds, Tottenham, Hull, Aston Villa and Coventry.

Furthermore, with Liverpool taking on Chelsea next weekend, Barcola and/or Mac Allister would be suspended for the trip to Stamford Bridge if either are booked against the Black Cats.

Ronald Araujo, Milos Kerkez and Virgil van Dijk are on three yellow cards, while Jeremy Jacquet and Munoz are among a host of Liverpool players still in danger of being suspended.

#1690. Gary Neville slaps himself in the FACE in bizarre on-air moment after Man United's humiliation at Anfield - weeks after claiming his old club are 'in a better place' than Liverpool

Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026

Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.

Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.

Instead, Man United saw their numbers reduced inside the opening stages of the game after a reckless challenge by Leny Yoro, and 2-0 down after 13 minutes, with the club legend resorting to drastic methods to convey the side's weaknesses.

Of his old club's defenders, he said: 'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'

Gary Neville took to slapping himself to convey the lack of focus he sees in Man United's stars

The club legend had previously tipped his old side to have a stronger XI than Liverpool's

But when the two teams met at Anfield, Man United were left woefully exposed after going down to 10 men

The Overlap broadcaster then slapped his own face a number of times repeating 'wake up!' before adding: 'You play for Man United'.

The gesture left Carragher in stitches, with the Anfield icon collapsing onto the sofa in hysterics - although less impressed with Roy Keane, who displayed his usual sangfroid.

So tickled by the moment was the former Liverpool star that he later changed his profile picture on social media site X to a still image of Neville's hand catching his face.

Neville had more sharp criticism for Man United's defensive selection assessing the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in the starting line-up.

The Dutch defender has been out of Premier League action for 51 weeks after suffering a back injury, but was named by Mauricio Pochettino in his first-ever XI.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him,' Neville admitted. 'It's like playing football after having six pints. It's a strange feeling.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him, it's alarming to watch.'

Less sympathy for Man United's players came from Keane, who attacked the team - and Neville and Carragher - after the heavy defeat at Anfield confirmed the club's worst start in over 53 years.

The firebrand midfielder was on his usual caustic form as he assessed the damage, hitting out at those who might have accepted the score line, having feared a greater deficit.

'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'

The difference between the two teams felt a far cry from Neville's late-summer prediction, when he told Carragher that he had greater hopes for Carrick and Man United over incoming manager Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

'I think Manchester United are currently in a better place than Liverpool,' Neville said in August. 'Would you agree?'

Carragher said that he did not, and will have been confident in his assessment on Sunday night.

#1688. Manchester United have new suspension risk after Leny Yoro red card appeal

Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for selection against Brentford this weekend, though a fellow defender remains at risk of a Premier League suspension.

Yoro was dismissed after just eight minutes in Man United’s defeat to Liverpool last Sunday, as Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after succeeding Michael Carrick as head coach quickly turned into a nightmare.

The Frenchman was given his marching orders for bringing down Alexander Isak just outside the box, with the Premier League revealing the red card was shown to the United defender “for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO)”.

However, Man Utd appealed the decision and it has proven successful with Yoro cleared to face Brentford on Saturday.

A statement from the FA read: “Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.”

Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal

United have had to deal with their fair share of suspensions already this season. Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matheus Cunha and, more recently, Youri Tielemans, have all been sent-off at some point to raise concerns over a disciplinary issue within the squad.

A further suspension concern is in the form of central defender Harry Maguire, who is currently on four Premier League yellow cards.

As per the rules, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Man United's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the away game against Brighton on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

Even if Maguire avoids a yellow card, he will still be walking the disciplinary tightrope in upcoming games against Newcastle, Coventry, Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Brighton.

The other Man United players in danger of a Premier League ban are Bruno Fernandes, Diogo Dalot, Ayden Heaven, Bryan Mbeumo, Andrey Santos and Luke Shaw, all on two yellow cards.

#1687. Barcelona release Alejandro Balde statement as ankle injury for Spain international is confirmed

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:14, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:16

Barcelona have revealed that Alejandro Balde suffered "a mild strain in his right ankle" during Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sabah.

Balde was handed a rare start against Sabah in the European Cup, but he had to leave the field in the 64th minute of the contest due to an ankle issue.

Barcelona have revealed that the Spain international suffered "a mild strain", but it is still possible that he could be involved in Sunday's La Liga match with Deportivo La Coruna.

“First-team player Alejandro Balde has a mild sprain in his right ankle. He is not ruled out for this Sunday’s match against RC Deportivo. His availability will depend on his recovery," read a statement from Barcelona.

It has been a frustrating campaign for Balde, who has only made six appearances in all competitions for the Catalan giants.

The defender has only featured for 100 minutes in Spain's top flight this season, while he has played 88 minutes of football in the Champions League.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Balde's future ahead of the January transfer window, with the left-back potentially being allowed to leave.

Manchester United continue to be linked with the 23-year-old, who has a contract at Camp Nou until the end of the 2027-28 campaign.

A loan move is most likely, should Balde move on in January, but a permanent departure has not been ruled out at this stage.

Barcelona are set to welcome Lamine Yamal back into their squad on Sunday, with the Spain international expected to recover from the ankle issue that ruled him out of the clash with Sabah.

Andreas Christensen and Rodri could also potentially return from injuries, but Xavi Espart and Roony Bardghji remain on the sidelines, while Fermin Lopez will be unavailable for selection through suspension.

#1686. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. But the Arsenal man hesitates and the keeper spreads himself, blocking Madueke’s eventual shot. He can’t turn around to get on the rebound and cuts is back for Tzolis, whose own shot is then blocked.

With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

Rice loses the ball in midfield and fouls Olivera as he tries to recover it.

Before they take the free kick though, Arsenal make more changes. Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke come on for Gyokeres and Saka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Sums up the game so far really for Arsenal.

There is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

There are the subs, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are the ones to make way.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

At the same time, Favasuli makes a neat little run on the right trying to get to the touchline and pull the ball back, but Raya is able to pick it up easily.

That was almost it for Napoli, Hojlund with a great run in behind. He gets into the box one-on-one against his defender as Raya retreats. The challenge is perfectly timed though as he tries to get his shot off and the ball goes spinning off to the side.

Neither side are looking clinical in front of goal though as Arsenal take the ball down the other end, and Declan Rice can only send another shot over the bar.

Saka tries to take another chance on the edge of the box, but he loses the ball.

Napoli try to seize their moment on the break, with Favasuli releasing down the left side. He looks for Hojlund in the middle of the field, but his cross is just not good enough and Raya comes out to collect the high ball.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

Though the hosts came out on the front foot, it has been all Arsenal since then, so Allegri will be hoping these changes can shift the momentum.

Alisson Santos gets past White on the sideline, and makes the run down the left. He tries to find De Bruyne making the run in the middle but it is intercepted and Arsenal take the ball back up the field.

Napoli are getting ready to make some changes.

Arsenal probing again, with Rice, Saka, Odegaard and White exchanging passes on the right edge of the box. Saka tries a low ball in but it’s blocked before it gets to Gyokeres.

Napoli are sitting so deep, you have to assume they are just waiting for an opportunity to counter. Even so, Arsenal are doing well to keep the ball moving around and try and find space. The hosts are really trying not to concede first.

Another wasted chance for Arsenal! Great play from Odegaard lifting a little ball into the centre of the box, which is flicked on towards goal. It falls to Hincapié in the six-yard box but as he tries to poke it into the goal, the Ecuadorian sends it flying over the bar.

Napoli have every man behind the ball right now as Arsenal get some possession.

Arsenal’s turn now, as White gets himself into a good position on the right side of the box, exchanging passes with Odegaard and Saka.

Saka tries to send a ball into the box, but it’s blocked and sent out the sideline as Napoli remain disciplined and shut down the space.

That momentum falls apart for Napoli as Oliveira fouls Gyokeres as the strikers comes in to defend.

Napoli are starting with some pressure here..

Napoli have changed their keepers at half-time. Meret received some treatment in the first half and has been taken off, replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. It’s his first appearance of the season.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

Reigning champions PSG are 3-0 up against Slovan, with a quick double coming from Mr Ballon D’or himself, Ousmane Dembélé. Ferran Torres scored the third.

Sporting vs Galatasaray also level at 1-1 so it’s really all to play for in the next 45 minutes. Stay tuned!

That’s the final action of the half, and nothing separates the two sides at the break. Both with three shots on target, though Arsenal have taken 13 shots to Napoli’s four.

Both teams could have stolen a goal to take the lead, but they will have to wait for the second period for the opportunity.

Arsenal get a corner which is delivered really well to the far post, but as it’s headed in, there is no space for White to turn and shoot from the six-yard box. He tries to lay it off for Hincapié but Meret gets low to grab it.

Arsenal have created more than enough chances to be three or four goals clear here. That miss by Saka was the best one yet, and the England winger will be in disbelief at the spooned nature of his finish. It looked a certain goal. Shocker.

Arsenal get another great chance as Odegaard sends a perfect ball to Saka as he makes the run into the box on the right side. The winger stays onside but Lobotka does enough to put him off and Saka sends it over the bar.

Napoli are first into the book as Gilmour fouls Eze 35 yards out.

Arsenal take the free kick but end up passing the ball around the edge of the box. Eventually Odegaard lifts a high ball into the box, but Meret punches it away confidently.

Konsa does really well to hold up Alisson Santos as he makes a very speedy run down the left, keeping him from sending a ball into the box.

The game is opening up now, as Saka makes a run of his own down the right, with Gyokeres in the box but Napoli keep tight and Rrahmani does well to stop the ball reaching the striker.

A good save from Raya as Hojlund again feeds the wings from the centre of the field. Politano makes a great run in from the right side with the ball and takes a curling shot with his left foot on the edge of the box.

Arsenal’s keeper collects and then minutes later his side have a shot of their own, but Saka can only send it over the bar.

Saka again gets enough time on the right edge of the box to send a low ball to Rice in the right corner. His shot goes over the bar and we’re having an impromptu drinks break as Meret gets some treatment.

Treat yourself to a hydration break of your own.

Napoli coming close as Hojlund fed in the centre, one-on-one with Konsa, trying to turn at the top of the box. He dinks the ball into the path of the running De Bruyne, whose shot is blocked by Konsa, who scrambles back quickly.

Hincapié sends a cross in from the left which almost catches Meret out at the near post as the keeper scrambles across to push it away.

Now it’s Napoli’s turn as Lobotka sends a long ball down the left to Alisson Santos, who sends a great cross in to the box. Konsa just does enough to put him off and it meets Rice in the centre of the box, for the midfielder to clear.

Saka comes in again on his left foot, with a series of short passes between Odegaard and Rice, but his shot is blocked as two defenders shut him down.

Another attempt for Arsenal as Odegaard gets forward and passes to Eze on the left wing. He drives in and takes a shot with his right foot from just inside the box, but he drags it wide of the target.

Good start to this game. Plenty going on. Arsenal look dangerous and capable of pinning Napoli deep into their own half, but the Italians have threatened on the break. De Bruyne’s shot from range would have triggered some nasty flashbacks for the Arsenal fans but, thankfully for them, it was straight at Raya.

Great chance from Arsenal as Eze pulls away at the back post and connects with the ball to send a header into the box. Merino connects with a diving header of his own but it’s straight at Meret and tipped over the bar.

Arsenal again biding their time until Rice plays a neat ball to White on the right edge of the boxm which he lifts into the box. No one around to do anything with it and Meret collects.

Arsenal being patient on the edge of the box moving the ball around, but eventually it breaks down with Eze losing the ball and then fouling De Bruyne as he tries to break away.

The Napoli players feel that should have been a card.

Di Lorenzo again looks to find space down the centre of the field but sends the ball out to Politano again on the right wing, who lofts a very high ball towards the back post but Raya collects with confidence.

Di Lorenzo makes a great run onto a long ball on the left side, racing down the sideline. He sends a ball across to find De Bruyne in the centre of the field, and the midfielder takes a great shot, which Raya can’t hold on to. White reacts to clear but Napoli are having a good spell.

Politano is the next to force a save from the Arsenal keeper with a shot from the right corner of the box, keeping their visitors very much on their toes.

Arsenal dominating possession in the early stages, just testing the Napoli defence. The stadium is quite quiet and we can hear the travelling fans declaring their love for their team.

Free kick for the visitors as Eze is fouled 40 yards out. Odegaard takes and sends a high ball into the centre of the box, which Gabriel can’t quite control.

Arsenal come again as Gyokeres sends a cross into the box from the left and Saka tries an overhead kick but it is straight into the centre of the goal and Meret has little trouble.

Rice again but the keeper comes to collect and sets the counter free.

Hojlund makes a great run and feeds Alisson Santos on the left side. He tries to cut in but is well marked by White and he can only send his shot over the bar from inside the box.

Arsenal get their first corner as Eze finds himself in a central position at the top of the box, and plays neat one-two with Gyokeres, but his shot takes a big deflection.

Rice goes to the corner flag, and sends in a good ball, headed out by Napoli for another corner.

Arsenal probing on the right wing, with White, Odegaard and Saka overlapping nicely. The captain feeds White and he passes in a neat little ball to Saka just inside the box. He tries a shot, but it’s blocked.

Napoli are getting back very quickly when Arsenal are pressing.

Marín sends a nice high ball across the field to find Politano on the right side. He feeds De Bruyne on the edge of the box and the Belgian tries a shot at Raya, curling it with his right foot, but with not much on it, Raya collects in the middle of goal.

Both teams getting little spells on the ball to get going.

Arsenal are keeping tight as Napoli try and play the ball out from the back and the long ball out to Hojlund is easily collected for Raya.

You can hear the Arsenal fans in loud voice, accompanied by plenty of jeers and whistles from the home fans.

The players are lining up around the centre circle, with a minute of silence for the victims of the tragedy in Nepal.

I wrote a little while ago that it was an unpleasantly warm evening in Naples. I now want to revise that comment. It’s nastily hot, and it’s getting worse. The air is thick (27 degrees and 74 per cent humidity, according to my weather app) and I can’t imagine it will be easy for the players.

As the players line up in the tunnel, here are the full teams in black and white:

Napoli starting XI: Meret, Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo, De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour, Santos, Hojlund, Politano

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola

Arsenal starting XI: Raya, White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Saka, Eze, Gyokeres

Subs: Kepa, Meslier, Tzolis, Madueke, Havertz, Calafiori, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman, Salmon

Here’s the TNT team on Arsenal’s left wing, which has been proving very effective so far this season as Calafiori, Tzolis and Hincapié have been finding their rhythm.

The players are warming up on the pitch, with 15 minutes to go before kick-off.

They are one of four 8pm matches, alongside:

Let us know how you think this one will go in the comments. Anyone fancying a Gyokeres hat-trick?

Barcelona managed to get five past Feyenoord, with recently departed Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus scoring the last goal minutes after coming on.

First goal for Barcelona 📞Gabriel Jesus bags Barcelona's fifth 🇧🇷 📺 Watch on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/TJmIhMkoXo

“Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

“We have to turn over a new leaf. We face a different challenge tomorrow. We’ll need to put in a technically excellent performance and be able to defend better than we did against Como and Inter.”

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

“It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Good evening from a very sticky and humid Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where the temperature is just a little too high to be pleasant. Perhaps that will change in time for kick-off. Perhaps it’s not relevant if I feel a bit uncomfortable in my jeans. Readers can make their own minds up on that…

Anyway, this should be a fun game. The atmosphere is usually pretty intense in this part of the world and they will be up for this one. The absence of Scott McTominay due to a minor heart problem is good news for Arsenal, who are likely to make a few changes to the team that beat Chelsea so impressively at the weekend.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they currently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

Despite the carnage at UK airports this week, Sam Dean has made it to Naples and will be bringing us updates from the continent.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Moises Caicedo starts for Chelsea in tonight’s Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest.

While Caicedo is fit to face Forest, neither Joao Pedro nor Maxence Lacroix are available.

Jordan Henderson, Pedro Neto and Danny Welbeck are also drafted in as Alonso makes three changes from the loss to Leeds.

It remains unclear exactly when Joao Pedro, Jorrel Hato or Lacroix will return, amid suggestions that the latter could be back before the start of 2027.

Winger Jamie Gittens, meanwhile, has been building his fitness of late having resumed training following an ankle injury.

However, the Portuguese impressed with his first words and was backed heavily in the summer – something which he arguably lacked at Old Trafford – and results have been largely positive.

#1683. Leeds vs. Coventry: Head-to-head record and past meetings

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 19:15, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 21:15

Elland Road will stage Saturday afternoon's Premier League contest between Leeds United and Coventry City.

Both teams enter this fixture after picking up maximum points last weekend, with Daniel Farke's side securing an impressive 4-1 victory at Chelsea and Frank Lampard's men beating Crystal Palace 3-2 on home soil.

Leeds have climbed to seventh in the Premier League table after 11 matches, while Coventry currently sit 14th and three points above the relegation zone.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

Leeds United and Coventry City have faced each other a total of 87 times across all competitions, and it is the Whites who lead the head-to-head record with 45 wins to the Sky Blues' 19, while 23 draws have also been played out.

November 1920 was the first time these two sides butted heads in the old Division Two, with both teams sharing the spoils in a 1-1 draw on Coventry's turf. Leeds responded with a thumping 4-0 home victory in the reverse fixture just a month later, but the Sky Blues got their revenge almost two years later with a slender 1-0 home success.

Leeds won 11 of their 18 Division Two encounters with Coventry (D2 L5), before both teams locked horns in Division One for the first time in November 1967, with a 1-1 draw played out at Elland Road.

The Whites then enjoyed a eight-game winning league run over Coventry up until October 1971 when they lost 3-1 away from home. Leeds responded by putting together a run of nine games unbeaten before the Sky Blues did the double over the West Yorkshire outfit in the 1976-77 campaign, winning 4-2 at home and 2-1 away.

Coventry's fortunes against Leeds improved between the late 1970s and late 1990s, posting five wins and seven draws in 17 games across all competitions (L5).

In the Premier League era (since 1992-92), Leeds and Coventry have faced each other 18 times in the top division of English football, with the Whites winning eight and the Sky Blues winning only three, with seven draws also recorded.

Coventry won two of their three Premier League meetings in the same season, with a 2-1 home victory in September 1996 followed three months later by a 3-1 away victory, courtesy of goals from Darren Huckerby, Dion Dublin and Gary McAllister.

These two wins for Coventry were part of a five-match winless Premier League run for Leeds in this fixture, but they have since won four and drawn two of their last six top-flight battles with the Sky Blues up until January 2001 (a 1-0 home win for Leeds in which Robbie Keane haunted his former club with the only goal of the game).

Each of the last 14 meetings between Leeds and Coventry have been in the Championship, with Leeds winning eight of those (D3 L3) including home (3-0) and away (2-0) victories in the 2024-25 season en route to securing promotion as champions under Daniel Farke.

#1682. Will Man City be stripped of Premier League titles? Possible sanctions amid new update before Arsenal showdown

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal take on Manchester City in the standout Premier League fixture this weekend, though it will be played in the backdrop of uncertainty.

While it is first against third and a showdown between last season’s top two, the outcome at the Emirates Stadium may not have too much of an impact on this year’s title race.

This is because Man City head to north London on the back of being handed an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges.

Back in October, City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018.

City, however, have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately launched with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should Man City’s appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.

Meanwhile, senior figures at some Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport that Man City’s owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for its breaking financial rules.

Below is a breakdown of what sanctions Man City could potentially face if their appeal is unsuccessful.

Expulsion from the Premier League: The most severe sanction could see Man City removed from the Premier League and relegated to the Championship, with any decision subject to the relevant league rules and the outcome of any appeal.

Suspension from Premier League matches: Another potential sanction would be a suspension. The club could potentially be suspended from participating in Premier League fixtures for a specified period.

More London travel chaos as weekend Tube and rail closures follow end of strike

Man Utd defender at risk of suspension after Leny Yoro red card appeal

Liverpool handed new suspension risk ahead of Chelsea clash

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Points deduction: A significant deduction in points could be imposed, either during the current season or in a future campaign.

The size and timing of any deduction would be determined as part of the sanctions process.

Stripping of titles and trophies: Retrospective sporting penalties could also potentially affect honours that were won during the period covered by the charges.

In this scenario, Arsenal would not be awarded a single retrospective Premier League title. This is because the seasons in which they finished runners-up to Man City has not been under investigation. The Gunners would, though get a League Cup after being demolished 3-0 by City in the 2017-18 final at Wembley.

However, no decision has been made to strip City of any titles or trophies.

Transfer restrictions: The club could potentially face restrictions on registering or signing players for one or more transfer windows.

Fines: City could also face substantial financial penalties. The club could be ordered to pay fines, compensation or costs associated with the proceedings.

The sanctions process is separate from the commission’s determination on the charges, meaning City’s punishment remains to be decided.

Enzo Kana-Biyik has trained with the Manchester United senior squad ahead of this weekend’s Premier League showdown against Brentford.

Man United welcome the Bees to Old Trafford on Saturday seeking a first league victory since August in what will be Mauricio Pochettino’s home debut as head coach.

The Red Devils go into the game in the relegation zone, but can climb out of the bottom three - albeit potentially temporarily - with victory coupled with Ipswich losing at home to Aston Villa.

#1680. Senne Lammens' Man United future called into doubt following Champions League clanger

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:37, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:39

Manchester United could look to bring in competition for number one goalkeeper Senne Lammens next year, according to former Red Devils captain Ashley Young.

Lammens has made a series of mistakes in recent matches and has only managed to keep one clean sheet for the Red Devils this season.

The Belgium international conceded a penalty against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday evening and then dropped a clanger late on to allow Luis Suarez to make it 2-2 in Portugal.

Lammens also made a high-profile mistake for Belgium at the 2026 World Cup against Spain, and Young has said that the 24-year-old may be on the verge of being dropped.

Young has even suggested that Man United could look to bring in competition for Lammens next year if his struggles continue.

Senne Lammens with a gift for Luis Suárez to equalise for Sporting ? ? Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/kOQ6HImlVc

"You look at the World Cup and the mistake he made, it's effected him massively. You just see it's mistake after mistake after mistake. He could be one mistake away from being dropped," Young told BBC Sport. "You've got Karl Darlow and Tom Heaton that are not really going to push Senne Lammens for that No.1 jersey, I do think Mauricio Pochettino is going to look and think 'If I can one of the keepers out of the door, and get someone in January to be pushing Lammens, then I will be doing that'. There's far too many mistakes."

Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino refused to criticise Lammens after the clash with Sporting despite the goalkeeper's unconvincing performance.

"This type of thing happens. That is football. Football is about making mistakes," Pochettino told reporters when asked about Lammens.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve - details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

Lammens arrived at Man United from Club Brugge in the summer of 2025, and he has represented the Red Devils on 49 occasions, conceding 74 goals and keeping just nine clean sheets.

The Belgian is expected to keep his spot between the sticks for Man United's Premier League clash with Brentford on Saturday afternoon.

Musiala has been restricted to just six appearances in all competitions this season, only two of which have been starts, due to a variety of issues.

Musiala did not return to action until September, but he subsequently suffered a torn muscle fibre in his right thigh while on international duty with Germany and returned to his club early.

#1677. Man United must build on improved Sporting Lisbon display in vital Premier League clash with Brentford

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:51, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:55

Manchester United will continue their Premier League campaign against Brentford on Saturday afternoon, and Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law has discussed all of the latest talking points surrounding the 20-time English champions.

Man United conceded the most goals, 36, the most penalties, five, and the most red cards, five, of any Premier League team this season.

The Liverpool game was controversial as well, with the red card for Leny Yoro that has since been rescinded. Isak does not have even a little bit of control of the ball. He has ballooned it 10 metres in front of him, and still, he is given the red card for that one.

That was a huge turning moment in the game. That is not to say that United should be going on and losing 4-0 at Anfield, even with 10 men, but it is a game-changing incident.

It leaves United on one Premier League win this season, down in 19th spot in the table, eight points from 11 games, which is absolutely horrendous. What I would say is it was a tough start for Pochettino. It was a big game at Anfield against the Liverpool side that played well.

If you concede that red card and then the fact they score from the free kick, that is a real hammer blow, and then you have to hold on and try to keep it 1-0 going into the second half.

United could not do that. The performance level was well off it again. They conceded four goals in each of their last two Premier League games. It is 23 goals conceded now in the Premier League in 11 games.

This team just cannot keep clean sheets for love nor money, in the Premier League, in any competition. Not kept a clean sheet since the win over Sabah in the Champions League, their first Champions League game in the league phase.

If you keep a clean sheet, you have got a really good chance of winning football games. If you concede two a game, three a game, you are just not going to pick up wins.

The game against Sporting Lisbon was one we could do a two-hour podcast on. The first penalty against Sporting is very soft.

If that is a penalty then we might as well pack up and do podcasts on something else, because I do not want to be a part of a game that says that is a penalty. The Senne Lammens one is a penalty. What is he doing? He is flying out.

Then the goal that was disallowed for Amad, how that is a foul from Tielemans I will never know. An absolute horrific decision. The Fernandes penalty is a penalty for me.

I think it is a straightforward decision. I do not think it is a foul on Senne Lammens, and I also do not think it is a foul for the last goal.

Dorgu got penalised for jumping into the goalkeeper, but they are either both fouls or neither are fouls. The contact on Senne Lammens for the Sporting equaliser was soft. I do not think that should be disallowed.

I do not think the United goal should be disallowed. The late red card was clumsy from Tielemans. It is not vintage football, it is not vintage Man United. They struggled in the final third of the field. Zirkzee came into the side and did okay.

An interesting stat from that game was that United had 12 high turnovers against Sporting, their most in any game this season.

It did feel like they were winning the ball back higher. They were definitely pressing more as a unit. The shape of the team was better. They need a centre forward. If they had had Sesko last night and that threat in behind, you feel like they could have picked up all three points.

They were decent on the ball, recovered well from going behind in the game. Sporting are a good side and have had good results in the Champions League this season.

They are a really strong team with really good players. There were positives from the Sporting Lisbon game, and it leaves them in a decent enough position in the Champions League.

They need to beat Leipzig in the next European game if they are really going to push on. They have got Bayern Munich and Villarreal as well, and those are going to be difficult games.

From the Champions League point of view, I still think they are in a decent enough position to finish in, whether that is the automatic qualification places or ultimately the play-offs.

Dealing with the Premier League is where they need to focus. They have got three games in a row now before the Leipzig game: Brentford, Newcastle away, Coventry at home.

The next two home games are absolutely massive. If they get turned over here and then go to Newcastle and do not manage to get a win, and then Coventry pick something up against them, it is very difficult.

I do not think United are getting relegated this season. I say that out of hope. I think they are going to be busy in January. They are going to have to be inventive.

Around £50m is the figure they are going to have to spend. They need to bring in three players: definitely a striker, definitely a centre-back, definitely a full-back.

Carlos Baleba is going to be back sooner than expected. They are going to hope to get Rashford back at some stage in the not-too-distant future. Those two did train in the gym ahead of the Sporting game. Shaw was back on the bench as well.

Pochettino said he was proud of his players for their performance level in the Sporting game and for overcoming the adversity, because there were some really horrific decisions from the referee and VAR in that game.

United have not had the rub of the green. With the Fernandes goal and the divot, they showed the earlier clip and it was Fernandes himself who had made that divot in the turf.

He had had a heavy touch with his boot in the box, and they circled back and it was the one he had made. So he actually managed to assist himself with that bobble. There has been a lot that has gone against United this season.

This is a really big game on Saturday afternoon and one I am hoping they can win against Brentford. First Premier League win for Pochettino. Go to the Newcastle game, can you get a point? Can you go there and beat Coventry? Can you beat Leipzig? Football changes very quickly. If you put three or four good results together, everyone feels different.

It goes in cycles. A big football match. Brentford, it is one of those games that back in the day, United at home to Brentford, you would think it is a gimme, a home win.

But they are an excellent team, Brentford, sitting sixth in the table at the moment with 17 points. Going away from home brings its different challenges, and without Igor Thiago as well is a big one.

I did also want to mention Senne Lammens' form, which is a concern for me.

Going back to the middle of September, Paul Scholes said in a podcast, The Good, The Bad and the Football, that he questioned whether Lammens was good enough, at a stage when he was actually playing quite well.

And I have to be honest, I am in that camp now. He is making a lot of mistakes.

There was one in the Sporting game last night where they did not concede from it, but he pushed the ball back into the middle and no one was on the rebound to put it away. The mistake for the second goal was a big one as well.

His form is slightly concerning and his confidence looks shot at the moment. I think he starts here, but it will be interesting to see whether United ultimately think they might have to get another goalkeeper in at some stage.

#1674. Mauricio Pochettino blames Man United's 'painful' thrashing at Liverpool on 'unfair' red card - after Roy Keane lashes out at Gary Neville for suggesting 4-0 defeat was an 'OK result' with 10 men

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER

Published: 16:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino suggested the Leny Yoro red card that had such an affect ontheir defeat by Liverpool game was 'unfair' and that their opponents should have been 'punished' too.

Pochettino gave up his job as US national team coach to join United on Wednesday, but any hope of a new manager 'bounce' evaporated after Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes and his team were thrashed 4-0.

It was the joint-heaviest defeat for a new United manager since Lal Hilditch a century ago, and leaves Pochettino's side second from bottom of the Premier League.

'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine, who blamed the early red card for United's defeat. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

'It's clear that after eight minutes the plan was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino blamed Leny Yoro's red card for his side's defeat by Liverpool

Yoro (right) was sent off for fouling Alexander Isak inside eight minutes of Sunday's game

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'

Pochettino was unhappy that referee Sam Barrott showed Yoro a straight red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak, having taken no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty box moments earlier.

'In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it,' added the United boss. 'If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper.

'If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth.'

He later added: 'One centre-back made a mistake and wasn't punished and us, we made one mistake and we were punished.'

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes agreed their team-mate should not have been sent off

United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with Pochettino that it wasn't a red card.

'No chance,' said Mainoo. 'The ball is already with the keeper, and they're both running full speed. What can he do?

'I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

'It's hard but no-one is going to save us. We have to come together and keep digging, keep fighting, and it will come round.'

Captain Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, added: 'I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card, and I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR with a long time to see, do it in slow motion, and make a mistake like this which can change the game.'

Gary Neville, who was left slapping himself in the face in shock live on Sky Sports, was pleased with damage control on, with United conceding four when it looked at one point that it would have been many more.

Former United captain Roy Keane, however, wasn't, and took aim at his ex-side's display.

'I thought United were desperate,' he said. 'So bad. Neville's OK with 4-0? Are you telling me they could have done better? 4-0 is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done.

Roy Keane (pictured), meanwhile, questioned why Gary Neville was pleased with the scoreline

'People who played for the club said 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish?

'Liverpool were excellent but how easy did United make it for them? This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

'Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'

#1673. Prediction: Hamburger SV vs Bayern Munich

Bayern Munich travel to the Volksparkstadion on Saturday aiming to put a difficult week behind them and reignite their Bundesliga title challenge against Hamburger SV.

The defending champions begin the weekend second in the table on 22 points, two behind leaders Borussia Dortmund, while Hamburg occupy 12th place with 12 points. Bayern will need a victory and a Dortmund slip-up if they are to end the round back at the summit.

Hamburg have generally enjoyed a positive campaign despite recent setbacks.

The Green-Whites have collected three more points after 10 Bundesliga matches than they managed at the same stage last season, evidence that progress is being made under Daniel Thioune.

However, results have taken a turn for the worse in recent weeks. Hamburg were heavily beaten 4-0 by Werder Bremen last weekend, and another defeat on Saturday could leave them just two points above the relegation zone.

Thioune’s side have now lost four of their last five matches in all competitions, scoring only five times while conceding 12 goals during that run. Those defensive struggles will be a major concern ahead of the visit of one of the division’s most dangerous attacking teams.

History also offers little encouragement. Hamburg have not beaten Bayern since July 2011, a sequence that has included 17 defeats and three draws.

Despite that record, home form has been respectable. HSV have won three of their five Bundesliga matches at the Volksparkstadion this season, although they have also suffered two defeats there.

Hamburg have been dealt a significant blow with midfielder Nicolai Remberg ruled out for the remainder of the season. His absence could see Nicolas Capaldo continue in central midfield.

In attack, Yussuf Poulsen is unavailable, meaning Patson Daka is expected to lead the line. He could be supported by Fabio Vieira, who is likely to feature in an advanced role.

Bayern arrive under unusual pressure after suffering their first defeat of the season.

The Bavarians were beaten 2-1 by Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, a result that followed a disappointing 1-1 Bundesliga draw against FC Koln. Those results have raised concerns that Bayern could lose further ground in the title race if they fail to respond quickly.

The defeat in France was also Vincent Kompany’s second match back on the touchline following his collapse in October, and the Belgian coach is still attempting to guide his side through a difficult spell.

Despite their recent frustrations, Bayern remain one of the Bundesliga’s strongest sides statistically. They have scored 30 goals in just 10 league matches, while only Borussia Dortmund have conceded fewer than their tally of 10.

The champions’ loss to Lille was their first defeat in any competition this season and also their first away defeat. Before that setback, Bayern had won six and drawn three of their first nine away matches.

Off-field issues have also generated headlines, with criticism directed at the club hierarchy over their handling of Jamal Musiala’s health situation, prompting Joshua Kimmich to publicly support his teammate.

Star striker Harry Kane is expected to miss several months with an ankle injury, while Michael Olise is a doubt for the trip to Hamburg.

There is better news regarding Luis Diaz, who should be available in some capacity, although Bayern may still be forced to deploy natural midfielder Konrad Laimer as their central attacking option.

Aleksandar Pavlovic was used in a more advanced role against Lille because of Bayern’s attacking injury crisis, but he is expected to return to midfield alongside Joshua Kimmich this weekend.

Hamburg may feel they are catching Bayern at a favourable moment given the visitors’ injury list and recent drop in form. The absence of Harry Kane in particular removes a huge source of goals, while Kompany’s side are still recovering from their first defeat of the campaign.

Even so, Bayern possess significantly greater quality throughout the squad and remain one of the Bundesliga’s most potent attacking outfits. Hamburg’s defensive record in recent weeks is another concern, particularly against opposition capable of creating chances in volume.

The hosts should put up a fight, but Bayern are expected to respond positively to a difficult week and leave Hamburg with all three points.

Prediction: Deportivo La Coruna vs Barcelona

Prediction: Borussia Dortmund vs Bayer Leverkusen

#1672. Real Betis vs Rayo Vallecano - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 20:17, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:19

Real Betis will be bidding to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume domestic affairs at home to Rayo Vallecano on Saturday afternoon.

The Seville outfit lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 21 victories to Rayo's 13, while 16 of their 50 previous matches have finished all square.

Real Betis will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-0 win over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League, with the result leaving them sixth in the overall table, claiming 12 points from their five games in the league stage of the tournament.

Manuel Pellegrini's side boast a record of eight wins, three draws and two defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 27 points leaving them in fourth spot in the La Liga table, five points ahead of fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

Real Betis are only four points behind third-placed Atletico Madrid, but they were held to a 1-1 draw by Sevilla in the Seville derby last weekend.

El Glorioso were last victorious in the league on November 8, beating Elche 2-0, while their last defeat at this level was a 5-2 home reverse to Barcelona on October 17.

Real Betis will be in Copa del Rey action against CD Extremadura on December 1 before facing Atletico Madrid in La Liga ahead of their next Champions League fixture with Como.

Rayo, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of successive defeats to Real Sociedad and Valencia in Spain's top flight, and it has been a tough season to date for the capital outfit.

Benat San Jose's side have a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 matches to sit in 16th spot in the division on 12 points, level on points with 18th-placed Getafe.

Rayo have the third-worst away record in Spain's top flight this season, picking up just two points from six matches, which is a concern ahead of this game.

Los Franjirrojos have actually drawn their last four matches against Real Betis, while they have not been beaten by the Seville outfit since September 2023.

The two teams played out a 1-1 draw in the corresponding game during the 2025-26 campaign, and it was also 1-1 when they locked horns in the same stadium in December 2024.

Real Betis remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension, while Dani Ceballos, Giovani Lo Celso, Iker Losada and Jose Morante are out through injury.

Cucho Hernandez scored twice against Slovan Bratislava on his return from injury on Tuesday evening, and the 27-year-old is now set to come in for his first league appearance since the middle of October.

Antony and Isco are both set to retain their spots in the final third of the field, while Pablo Fornals is likely to be joined by Marc Roca in the middle of the midfield.

As for Rayo, Augusto Batalla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin are out through injury, but the capital outfit have no fresh fitness concerns.

Sergio Camello has been in strong form this season, scoring seven times in 13 appearances, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be another spot at centre-forward for Randy Nteka despite the fact that the 28-year-old is still waiting for his first goal of the campaign.

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Fornals, Roca; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Hernandez

Audero; Ratiu, Lejeune, Sadick, Tsiaishvili; Palazon, Ciss, Lopez, De Frutos; Nteka, Camello

Rayo have found it difficult on their travels this season, and we are expecting Real Betis to secure all three points even though their preparation time for the match will be short.
